findings.title: CAUTION overstates when the rolling-updates feature is required
findings.body: The new CAUTION block states that the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled, 'Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' This is too broad. The companion test change in `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` enables the feature only when `spec.update.strategy` is explicitly set; the default case (no update strategy) deliberately deploys the Keycloak CR without the feature and still expects rolling-upgrade behavior for configuration changes (`testCacheMaxCount` with a null strategy asserts `eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus`). So the Operator only fails when `spec.update` is used without the feature, not in general. As written, the doc will scare users into enabling a preview feature they don't need for the default upgrade behavior. The caution should say the feature is required only when setting `spec.update.strategy`.

findings.title: Feature-disabled exit code 4 and the check command path are not tested
findings.body: This PR introduces a new exit code `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (and renumbers the recreate exit code from 4 to 3), making the exit code the documented contract for automation ('they should rely only on the exit code of the check command'). However, `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message text for the `metadata` subcommand; it never asserts that the exit code is 4, and it does not exercise the `check` subcommand with the feature disabled at all. A regression that returns exit code 0 or 1 when the feature is disabled — which would silently break GitOps pipelines that branch on this code — would not be caught. The test should assert `cliResult.assertError(...)` plus the exit code 4, and cover `update-compatibility check` without `--features=rolling-updates`.
